title: Chapter 11: Harvest
paragraphs: Seeing the Grand Formation resume its operation, Chen Mobai finally breathed a sigh of relief.At this point, I hope readers will remember our domain: sto55.com.
He wanted to sit down and rest, but the sight of the two corpses in the Water Abode completely ruined his mood.
Every time he closed his eyes, he could still see their faces, frozen in death with their eyes wide open.

Chen Mobai had no experience dealing with corpses. He paced back and forth in the main hall, noticing the dead fish. He considered tossing the bodies into the water outside the Grand Formation, letting the fish devour them clean.
But after careful thought, he shook his head.

Though he didn't know exactly where this Eastern Barrens was, he had been obsessed with crime dramas since childhood. He doubted the fish here were ferocious enough to completely destroy the bodies and erase all traces.

To prevent the corpses from surfacing and being discovered by Eastern Barrens cultivators, leading them to this place, Chen Mobai concluded that the safest course of action was to thoroughly eliminate all evidence of their existence within the Water Abode itself.
But how to do that?

Chen Mobai paced back and forth, his brow furrowed in worry. He considered burning the body, but even if he possessed a fire-based cultivation technique—which he didn't—and could generate sufficient heat, the thought of a mere high school student like himself incinerating a corpse in this confined space was simply beyond his capabilities.
Finally, he stood before the old man's mangled remains, suppressing his body's instinctive revulsion. Just as he was about to turn away, his gaze fell upon the sealed stone gate of the Side Hall.
"That's it! I can use the Restriction here."
Recalling how a coin he'd tossed to test the gate had been vaporized by the eerie blue electrical discharge, Chen Mobai felt his plan might work.
Without hesitation, he acted.
Truth be told, Chen Mobai couldn't bear to remain near the corpse any longer.
Using his most practiced Lightness Technique, he levitated one of the old man's arms and flung it toward the stone gate of the Side Hall.

As expected, without any Spiritual Power or protective barrier, the bloodstained arm was instantly vaporized into a crimson mist by the blue electrical discharge, staining the floor tiles and triggering the Restriction's power through the blood splattered on the stone gate.
The entire Water Abode was now immersed in the flickering, pulsating glow of electricity.
After five cycles of this process, the old man's corpse had finally been completely incinerated.
To Chen Mobai's surprise, the Restriction on the Side Hall's stone gate seemed to have weakened slightly.
It appears the Side Hall's Restriction isn't connected to the Water Abode's Spiritual Vein. Breaking it will be much easier now.

Skilled formation masters would typically link crucial structures within a defensive Grand Formation to the Spiritual Vein itself. This way, even if the Restriction on a building were weakened, it would immediately regenerate as long as the Grand Formation remained intact and the Spiritual Vein flowed.
While the Azure Water Grand Formation was decent, it was clear the formation master had merely purchased a Formation Plate and Array Flags, then set them up according to the instructions.

After disposing of the old man's remains, Chen Mobai noticed a bloodstained cloth pouch on the floor. Acting cautiously, he used the Lightness Technique to levitate the pouch, then telekinetically dumped its contents onto the ground.
A clattering pile spilled out:
A dozen neatly cut gold bars, two books, three bottles of Medicinal Pills, a short dagger, and a set of spare robes.

Chen Mobai's breathing quickened as he saw the gold. Though its value was less than in the previous civilization, it remained a valuable cultivation material within the Immortal Sect. Whether used as gold powder for writing talismans or refined into gold essence, it commanded a strong market.
Roughly estimating, these dozen or so gold bars were worth over eight hundred Merit Points. If handled skillfully, they could yield nearly a thousand.
Having never possessed such wealth before, Chen Mobai's heart stirred with excitement.

He picked up the two books and flipped through them. One appeared to be the old man's cultivation manual, titledBlackwater Art. Chen Mobai glanced at it before setting it aside; now wasn't the time to study this.
The other book's title made his breath catch in his throat:
Detailed Explanation of the Azure Water Grand Formation: From Novice to Mastery

This was the manual for the very Grand Formation guarding the entire Water Abode! Chen Mobai had initially dismissed the old man's claim of being the Water Abode's master's disciple as a lie. But seeing this book, he began to wonder if it might be true after all.
The Formation Manual was quite thick. Chen Mobai glanced at his phone and saw that he only had an hour before class, so he decided not to study it in detail for now.
At that moment, another question occurred to him: could he take all these items with him when he returned to the city?
With this question in mind, he began dealing with the brown-robed youth's corpse.
Now experienced, he first used the Lightness Technique to flip the body over. As expected, he found six hidden pockets in the youth's sleeves.
Inside were a bottle of Medicinal Pills, two jade-white stones, a foldable crossbow, and a Flying Needle Sect disciple's manual.

Next, he opened the palm-sized Needle Case in the youth's hand and collected the earth-yellow Flying Needles scattered everywhere. Chen Mobai then contentedly gathered the contents of the old man's pouch and piled them together.
After vaporizing the corpse again using the Stone Gate Restriction, Chen Mobai used the old man's spare robes as rags to wipe away all traces of blood throughout the Water Abode.
The floor tiles before the Side Hall's entrance had been meticulously cleaned of bloodstains using the Lightness Technique to remotely manipulate his robes. Even the fish had been retrieved.
Everything was restored to pristine order, giving Chen Mobai the satisfying sense of accomplishment one feels after tidying up one's home.
He plopped down in the middle of the main hall, facing the pile of hard-earned spoils he had painstakingly gathered.

The old man's cloth bag was stained with blood, which Chen Mobai considered inauspicious and discarded. He removed his upper robe, spread it over the floor tiles, and then carefully arranged the items on top.

Finally, his hand brushed against the two jade-white stones. A gentle, pure Spiritual Energy surged through the meridians in his palm like a warm current, sending a shiver down his spine. He nearly cried out in pleasure.
"This... could it be... Spirit Stones?!"
If the previous items had merely excited Chen Mobai, these two jade-white stones completely threw him off balance.
In the Immortal Sect, these stones were as precious as gold had been to the previous civilization on Diyuan Star—priceless treasures beyond measure.

At the same time, due to Diyuan Star's scarce resources, all Spirit Stone mines had long been thoroughly surveyed and explored. Except during times of war, mining Spirit Stones was strictly prohibited.
Yet even with these restrictions, according to the Immortal Sect's latest financial report, the entire Diyuan Star's Spirit Stone reserves were critically low.

If not for a genius who emerged from the Immortal Sect two thousand years ago and invented a miraculous technique—infusing dried-up Spirit Stones with Spiritual Energy to restore them to eighty percent of their original, newly mined state—the Immortal Sect's Merit Point system would have collapsed long ago due to a lack of Spirit Stones for redemption.
Even so, the Immortal Sect only permitted cultivators to exchange Merit Points for Spirit Stones at the bank during times of war.
Ten thousand Merit Points were equivalent to one low-grade Spirit Stone.
